body.x: Spaid (CEO Chongkul Yi) has announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will showcase groundbreaking solutions under its vision of connecting physical and digital environments to maximize the utility of live information and data.

Focusing on “one-of-a-kind" innovation, Spaid integrates diverse datasets from the public and private sectors to generate actionable insights for smarter decision-making. The company offers Geospatial AI solutions that serve industries such as smart cities, digital twin operations, defense simulations, real estate value analysis, building energy management, financial risk management, and telecommunications resource optimization.

At CES 2025, Spaid will present its CES Innovation Award-winning solution, AI2RE ("Image-Based 3D Geospatial Metaverse"), and a demo of its upcoming "OpenAI-Powered Geospatial Information Platform," slated for release in the first half of 2025.

AI2RE employs a proprietary AI engine to extract 2D vector lines from aerial imagery (satellites, drones, etc.) and generate 3D terrains, buildings, and road models. By automating over 80% of the traditional processes, AI2RE overcomes data loss and compatibility challenges, offering reliable 3D geospatial information for governments and enterprises. The solution has already demonstrated its efficacy in European Union data management projects, reducing geospatial mapping efforts from six months per person to just five days. It is being considered for applications in South America and Africa.

Spaid will unveil its OpenAI-Powered Geospatial Information Platform at CES for the first time. This platform allows users to receive tailored geospatial data cards via OpenAI agents and intuitively visualize and analyze 3D maps without additional tools or software. By integrating global datasets, Spaid is developing a roadmap for creating a digital twin metaverse applicable to real-world industries.

CES attendees visiting Spaid’s booth can experience the AI2RE solution and the OpenAI-Powered Geospatial Information Platform. The interactive demonstrations will showcase real-time object recognition, 2D line extraction, 3D modeling processes, and hands-on visualization of San Francisco's geospatial data cards in a 3D map viewer.

Chongkul Yi, CEO of Spaid, expressed his pride in receiving the CES Innovation Award and emphasized the company’s commitment to showcasing cutting-edge solutions in geospatial AI and the metaverse. We aim to accelerate our entry into global markets by demonstrating the excellence of our innovative technologies at CES 2025," he said.
